title: Restocking shelves
summary: How shelf stock works in Supermarket Simulator: you buy stock, carry it from the storage room and fill the shelves yourself, and a product can be locked behind a store level.
body: Shelves only sell what you put on them. Stock arrives from the storage room, not from the shelf, so a normal loop is: order or carry boxes in, unpack at the shelf, and refill before the shelf runs empty.
Products are not all available from the start. Each product can carry a required store level, which is why some items cannot be ordered until the shop has grown.
What this entry does not tell you: prices, order quantities, restock timings and how fast customers buy. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The game runs an automated restock loop for shelves.
facts.evidence: identifier in the game's own files: ProductRestockLoop

facts.claim: A product can require a minimum store level before it is available.
Shelves can be refilled automatically when a slot is empty.
Products are identified by their own product id.
The build names its shelving by pattern and width, including a bakery shelf in a single and a standard width.
